correctness.rationale: For G=GP(8,3) with 16 vertices and 24 edges, the complete finite complex has f-vector (16,96,272,376,240,72,16,2), 1090 nonempty faces and 4272 Hasse covers. An independently implemented greedy matching yields 542 pairs, is acyclic on all faces, and leaves one critical 0-face, four critical 3-faces and one critical 4-face. Exact integer elimination gives Morse d4=(0,0,0,0), so H3=Z^4 and H4=Z and other positive homology vanishes. Independent full boundary-rank elimination modulo 3 yields (15,81,191,181,58,14,2), compatible with exact integral certificate. Independent oriented fixed-simplex traces for the eight powers of the canonical rotation give L=(-2,0,2,0,-2,0,2,0). A nonboundary degree-four mod-3 cycle transforms to minus itself modulo degree-five boundaries (and not plus), so the integral rank-one H4 action must be sign. Consequently chi3=1+chi4-L=(4,0,0,0,4,0,0,0), chi4=(1,-1,1,-1,1,-1,1,-1), giving the rational C8 decomposition 1 ⊕ sign ⊕ Q[x]/(x²+1). This is an exhaustive finite theorem for the stated graph, not a family extrapolation.
residual_risks: Homology module decomposition is rational only; no full Aut(G) representation, integral C8-lattice classification or equivariant homotopy type is established.
Original verifier output alone was not taken as evidence; an independently written finite-complex/rank/Morse/character computation was performed.

value.rationale: The canonical order-eight rotation is intrinsic to the G(8,3) model of a highly symmetric 16-vertex cubic graph. A full C8-character calculation distinguishes the negative action on its unique H4 generator and an order-four rational 2-dimensional summand of H3, data invisible to the already known 4-sphere Betti summary. This is a natural, bounded and independently useful equivariant invariant and gives a benchmark for future full automorphism-module calculations; it does not need to imply a larger theorem to matter.
residual_risks: The classification is a single canonical cyclic subgroup of one graph; it is not the full order-96 automorphism representation.
The same-object nonequivariant homotopy type is previously known, and its determination is not claimed as new.
